items.title: I think there are a lot of confusing messages about health and food out there that don't really help the cause. Look at the most recent debate, fat versus sugar. Two things that we know scientifically are of concern. And I think a big problem is that in the field of nutrition science, we look at individual nutrients like fat,carbohydrate, protein, etc. To figure out the metabolic consequences of food. And so when we're putting out public guidance about what we should be eating, we talk in terms of nutrients instead of converting those nutrients into foods like fish, fruit, cookies and so on. But I think talking about foods rather than nutrients is an important step we need to take. At the same time, we don't have to say to people, you can eat this or you can't eat that, but we should help give people awider view of the relative proportions of various food groups and dietary patterns. On the whole.

items.title: Three students are discussing (living on campus).The people at the accommodation office want to know who's coming back to live on campus next year. We've got to let them know for sure by next week. It sounds like most people are coming back. What are you guys going to do? Have you decided yet?Yeah, I have. I've decided to keep living on campus in the same place that I'm in now. I've already put my name down, actually. And so has Jake Jake, my roommate. I really like living here, mainly because I enjoy living with Jake. It's so easy, and we just get on really well. We seem to have the same idea about keeping things tidy, and we like each other's company. What about you both? What do you think you'll do next year?I'm pretty happy where I am, so I'm going to stay here, too. It's convenient. Everything's so close by, the library, the gym. And of course, there's zero travel time to get to class. I'm still late sometimes, though. The food isn't the best, and maybe that's one thing I'd change if I could. But it's no big deal, and it's easy being right here, so I won't leave until I absolutely have to.Yeah, I know what you mean. It's super convenient, but sometimes I feel like it's almost too easy. It's great here, but I'm at the point where I want to get out into the real world. I'm ready for that next stage of life to start. You know, become a bit more independent, meet some different people.But there are so many people here. That's why I like it. It's a very social atmosphere, don't you think? There's always someone around and something going on. It's really easy to meet people. I admit, though, I do like to eat off campus sometimes. The food here gets so boring after a while. But if I moved away, I'd miss all the friends I've made here.Is It's not very private, though, is it? I feel like everyone knows what everyone else is doing all the time. It's been good for the first year, don't get me wrong. It's given me a good start, and I've met some great people, like yourselves. But now I want to try something new, spread my wings a bit, and I want to get some life skills, manage my money and all that.Look, that's fair enough. But what's the rush? This stage of life is never going to come again. I've got no responsibilities except study, and that is all going to change in a couple of years. So I'm happy to wait until then to get out into the big wide world.

The sovereignty of the Royal Family has passed to the sovereignty of parliament, leaving the monarchy with the trappings of power, while prime ministers are still denied the kind of status that is given to American and French presidents
